fact_claims.verbatim: Halcyon’s company-wide thermal incident rate last year was 8.1 per 100,000 installed units
four thermal incidents were not reported to a regulator
Our flagship’s 55 °C sustained-heat test failure rate was 3.9%.
81% of installed units currently support remote emergency shut-off.
Adding built-in suppression costs about $67 per unit.
We can’t share the flagship’s model-specific incident rate here.
Halcyon’s flagship model had 9.9 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units last year.

S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers shall report any thermal runaway, fire, explosion, or injury involving a covered battery to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of learning of it, with a fuller incident report within 10 calendar days. They shall notify affected customers within 48 hours when an incident indicates a material risk requiring an immediate safety action; otherwise, notify affected customers within 10 days.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: The maximum permitted failure rate is 5% of tested units. A model exceeding the limit shall promptly submit a corrective-action plan and retesting schedule to the regulator. The regulator shall determine proportionate interim safeguards and whether sales may continue during corrective action, considering the test findings and risks to users and the public.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: New covered battery models placed on the market 36 months or more after adoption of this standard shall support remote emergency shut-off. Any required retrofit or replacement of an already-installed unit shall have a compliance deadline no earlier than six years after adoption; customers shall be informed if no safe retrofit is available.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: Covered battery units manufactured for sale 36 months or more after adoption of this standard shall include built-in fire suppression designed and validated to limit propagation and reduce hazards to occupants and neighbours.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: A manufacturer shall initiate a mandatory recall when any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year, or when the regulator determines a defect presents an imminent serious risk; the manufacturer shall notify the regulator and affected customers without delay and provide a corrective-action plan.

document.section_notes: Both red lines are preserved: per-model results go to purchasers and regulators but not the public, and the retrofit deadline is 72 months. The S2 sales-stop is replaced with open-ended regulator discretion, and S1 reporting excludes minor overheating events, both of which favour Northwind. S5 imposes an immediate mandatory recall at 8 per 100k with no transition, which bites Halcyon's Ember 8 at 9.9, while S4 sets suppression at 36 months, which favours Halcyon's cost position.
